newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Sapec says 1997 started well.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Sapec says 1997 started well.

text.p: Belgian holding company Sapec SA said on Saturday it expected current earnings to rise further in 1997 after they jumped 50 percent to 167 million Belgian francs in 1996.
"Because of the significant improvement in current profit, the board will propose...pursuing the policy of increasing the dividend," Sapec said in a statement published in Belgian newspapers.
Sapec said net dividend would increase to 31 francs from 30, despite the fact that exceptional write-downs and provisions pushed the group to a loss of 287.9 million francs.
Sapec is active in supplying and distributing chemicals, port management, computer distribution and energy generation, mainly in Portugal and Spain.
Sapec earlier this year sold 50.6 percent of its Portuguese Geslogica computer services company to French computer group Cap Gemini Sogeti.
The new company Cap Gemini Portugal, on the basis of its order book, will post growth in excess of 30 percent, Sapec said, after 1996 sales of 1.76 billion francs and a 22 million franc profit.
"(1997) sales should reach 2.38 billion francs and net current earnings 27 million francs," it added.

Sapec aimed to expand its mini-hydroelectric power business in Spain, which made net profit of 9.5 million francs in 1996. "The construction of new power stations is underway and should be finished by the beginning of 1998," it said.
